title: Influence of the two-coordinate indicator
statement: Let $X_0,X_1$ be independent and uniform on the three-point set $\{a,b,c\}$, and let $F(X_0,X_1)$ equal $1$ when both coordinates are $c$ and $0$ otherwise. The squared $L^2$ norm of the difference between $F$ and its average over coordinate $0$ is $\frac{2}{27}$.
